page: Microsoft Azure F32amds_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine from the Famdsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a capacity of 3780 GB, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. It does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong compute and memory capabilities. The single-core CPU performance under stress-ng and single-threaded gzip compression both rank in the top tier (top 10%). Multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth (both read and write) fall into the strong category (top 25%). For database operations, Passmark database benchmarks place this server in the top tier (top 10%), supported by strong Redis SET operations. Large-model LLM inference (70B model) drops to average performance (middle 50%), while smaller models (135M) achieve top-tier processing speeds.

The high memory density and substantial local storage capacity offer qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound and data-intensive workloads, reducing the need for external storage overhead. The absence of a GPU limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, but the high-frequency AMD EPYC processor and large memory capacity make it suitable for relational databases, in-memory caching, data analytics, and medium-scale language model inference.
